key_insight: The paper proposes a fair classification method that enables post-hoc control of the fairness–accuracy trade-off while avoiding retraining and preserving strong trade-off efficiency.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for deployed ML systems where fairness requirements may change over time, since operators can adjust fairness settings after training with minimal compute overhead.
method: Learns feature representations that make post-processing fairness adjustments more effective.
Uses a gradient-based optimization approach during training.
Combines the flexibility of post-hoc control with efficiency comparable to in-processing methods.
evidence_signal: Experiments on real-world datasets show the method achieves trade-off efficiency comparable to, or better than, in-processing approaches without retraining.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the learned representation, so implementation and tuning may be important for consistent fairness–accuracy behavior.
paper_title: Fair Classification with Efficient and Post-hoc Controllable Fairness-Accuracy Trade-off
